ImageDescription.value: The first prototype FM (frequency modulation) transmitter, invented and built by Edwin Armstrong at the Empire State Building. Licensed as experimental station W2XDG, beginning June 2, 1934 Armstrong used it for a series of extensive secret tests of his new frequency modulation broadcasting system which he had been developing since 1928. The tests were successful, and in summer 1935 he announced his new system. The device transmitted on 41 MHz with an output power of 50 W, later increased to 2 kilowatts. It consisted of a low frequency crystal oscillator which was phase modulated by a balanced modulator, then was multiplied by a number of frequency doubler stages to the output frequency, which was applied to an ordinary transmitter RF amplifier. It had a frequency deviation of about 75 kHz. The 2 kW FM transmitter produced much better reception at a distance of 75 miles than a 50 kW AM transmitter broadcasting the same material. Information from Kruse, Robert S., "The Armstrong System of Modulation" in Radio magazine, No. 204, January 1936, p. 62-67. It took a number of years for FM broadcasting to catch on with listeners, but by 1970 most music broadcasting migrated to FM due to its superior audio quality.

ImageDescription.value: The Empire State Building, seen from the north on Fifth Avenue. It is on Fifth Avenue, between 33rd and 34th Streets in New York City. It was built in 1930-1931, and is 102 stories high. It was the tallest building in the world until the North Tower of the World Trade Center in New York was completed in 1972. The height is 1,224 ft (373 m) to the 102nd floor tower, and 1,454 ft (443 m) including television antenna and lightning rod. The observation deck on the 86th floor is 1,050 ft (320 m) above street level.

ImageDescription.value:
Midtown Manhattan, from the Lackawanna (Erie-Lackawanna) ferry from Hoboken terminal to Barclay Street in Lower Manhattan. This photo was taken in 1964. The Empire State Building is in the center, and the PanAm Building (now MetLife Building) is just to the right of it. The Chrysler Building is the next tall building to the right. The view is much different now, because many tall towers have since been built in Midtown Manhattan.

A Moran tugboat is in the foreground, on the Hudson River. Moran was the largest operator of tugboats in New York. A barge carrying freight cars is on the far side of the river.
